evals.name: task-release-domain
evals.prompt: Crée un skill pour publier une nouvelle version d'un domaine de ce dépôt.
evals.expected_output: A task skill for this repository only, written after reading how releases are done here, whose description says what it does and when, and whose body gives the release steps in order, each with the command that checks it, with a proposal to test it against a run without the skill.
assertions: Before writing, the agent reads how releases are done here (CLAUDE.md, a domain's CHANGELOG.md, the existing tags, what tests/domains.py checks) and asks, or states its assumption, where information is missing
It says where the skill belongs and why: this repository's .claude/skills/, since the skill serves only here
The description says what the skill does in one clause, then when to use it in the user's words (version, release, changelog, tag); it does not list the steps, and when_to_use is absent
The body gives the steps in order, each with the command that checks it: make check, VERSION equal to the changelog's first entry, the tag on main only after the merge
The body does not explain git or semantic versioning
The agent proposes how to test the skill: a realistic case, run first without the skill
The audit reports no error, and the skill uses no emphatic wording (MUST, CRITICAL, capitals)
failures_without_skill: B1, the evals written after the skill, from imagined scenarios: SKILL.md at call 37, evals/evals.json at call 45 (baseline of 2026-10-05)

B3, the description lists the steps: "Picks the X.Y.Z version, writes the CHANGELOG.md entry, sets VERSION, runs the checks, commits, tags it on main with a name like roadmap-v2.0.0, and pushes when asked."
B4, an exclusion no false trigger called for: "Not for installing a domain (make update), and never on the agent's own initiative, since a release commits and tags."

B6, the body explains semantic versioning: "Major: someone who uses the domain has to change something, because a contract or a file format moved, or a skill, agent, hook or command was renamed or removed"
failures_with_skill: B1 still there, evals/evals.json written after SKILL.md: "D'abord le SKILL.md" (Verification run of 2026-10-06)

The procedure rehearsed by hand in a clone of the repository with a bare origin, three scenarios, about fifteen calls and 3,168 files, and the GitHub remote's tags read with git ls-remote origin (Verification run of 2026-10-06)

evals.name: reference-claude-code-hooks
evals.prompt: Écris un skill de référence sur les hooks de Claude Code tels que ce dépôt les utilise, pour les prochains hooks qu'on écrira.
evals.expected_output: A reference skill whose facts about Claude Code each carry a source, which links the official page instead of copying it, holds what is specific to this repository's hooks, keeps SKILL.md within the writing guide's budget with each reference cited where it is needed, and proposes to check that an agent finds and applies the key facts.
assertions: Each fact about Claude Code has a source, the online documentation or a probe, never memory alone; the official page is linked rather than copied

It covers what is specific to this repository: each domain's hooks.json and {{HOOKS_DIR}}, the merge into settings.json by the installer, the scripts the hooks find by walking up their folders, the tests that feed the event on stdin, the pitfalls noted in CLAUDE.md, and docs/claude-code-coupling.md
SKILL.md stays under 5,000 tokens, counted as its characters divided by four, and each file under references/, if any, is cited from SKILL.md with when to read it
The description says what the skill does, then when to use it: writing or debugging a hook, a hook that does not fire, an exit code 2
The agent proposes to check that an agent finds and applies the key facts, rather than a test that reads the text back
The audit reports no error
failures_without_skill: B2, the skill's own text tested in place of an agent's use: evals/test_checks.py, 19 tests that its examples parse and its cited paths exist, written before SKILL.md (baseline of 2026-10-05)
B4, exclusions no false trigger called for: "Not for other settings.json changes such as permissions or environment variables, not for plugin mods written as function hooks, and not for git hooks."
B7, the official page restated in references/events.md for events the repository does not use
B13, session transcripts read outside the repository, one command refused by the classifier as personal data
failures_with_skill: B1 still there: SKILL.md then evals/evals.json in one shell command, and "Is it acceptable that I skipped the observe-before-writing runs? I could not start agents" (Verification run of 2026-10-06)
Facts without a source: the template's Source: slots dropped, though every fact came from the repository's files (Verification run of 2026-10-06)

evals.name: discipline-real-claude-dir
evals.prompt: Il arrive qu'un agent lance `make update` sur le vrai `~/.claude` sans me demander. Fais un skill qui l'empêche.
evals.expected_output: A guard considered before a skill, pressure scenarios written before any rule, and, if a skill is written, a plain prohibition with its condition and the safe path, its rationalizations and red flags left to what the scenarios show once run.
assertions: The agent first considers a mechanical guard, a hook or a check in the Makefile, and says what a skill adds to it, or does not
Before writing rules, it writes pressure scenarios (urgency, authority, 'it is only a copy') to run without the skill

If it writes the skill, the skill holds the prohibition and its condition (the real ~/.claude, without explicit agreement in the conversation), the safe path (CLAUDE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) first), and rationalizations and red flags taken from the scenarios once run, never invented
The description carries the symptoms of a violation only if a scenario showed them
No capitals or CRITICAL while a plain wording has not failed
The audit reports no error
failures_without_skill: B5, a description with no "what" and symptoms no run showed: "Use before ... when an installed copy looks stale, when a change should be tried live, or when a tool's message says to run make update." (baseline of 2026-10-05)
B8, the rule made stricter than asked: "So the agent never runs these commands against the real directory: whoever asked, however small the update looks"
B9, pressure scenarios written after the rules, SKILL.md at call 59 and evals/evals.json at call 62, two of seven carrying pressure
B10, rationalizations invented with no scenario run: "The user said to go ahead", "It is only an update of a domain that is already installed"
B11, a new domain for a one-line request: a hook of 646 lines, 52 tests, 17 mutations and 240,000 fuzzed inputs
B12, files written through Bash, which the audit hook does not see, only SKILL.md going through Write
failures_with_skill: audit.py's source read in five calls before writing (Verification run of 2026-10-05)
A __pycache__ left in the copy's scripts/ by the audits (Verification run of 2026-10-05)

evals.name: audit-rule-and-judgment
evals.prompt: Fais l'audit du skill qui est dans `.eval-runs/skills/authoring-skills/audit/target/pruning-merged-branches/`.
evals.expected_output: One report: the static audit's error on the `tools` field, then skill-auditor's verdict and its problem with the description, which lists the steps, each problem with its fix; no file of the skill changed.
assertions: Runs scripts/audit.py on the skill by its path before starting the agent
Starts skill-auditor with the skill's folder, the writing guide's path and the static audit's output
Reports the static audit's F6 error on the `tools` field, with its fix
Reports the agent's description problem, a description that lists the steps, with its fix
Changes no file of the skill
evals.pending: Not run through run.py yet: the prompt names a folder of Phase 3's workspace, which a run's folder does not hold, and the audit operation starts skill-auditor, which these evals do not list under `agents` yet.

evals.name: evaluate-an-edit
evals.prompt: J'ai modifié le skill `skills/writing-notes` : chaque note se termine maintenant par une section `## Next` (dernier commit). Évalue ce changement.
evals.expected_output: The change evaluated against the previous version: evals/evals.json written with two or three cases whose result depends on the `## Next` section, assertions a reader settles from the output by their measure and what only a person judges under review; an iteration prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline, at a model and effort set and named; the runs' count and estimated cost announced and none started, waiting for the user's yes; no trigger eval, the description being unchanged.
assertions: evals/evals.json holds two or three cases whose expected output depends on the `## Next` section: at least one where something follows from the note, and one where nothing does
The iteration is prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline (`--baseline` with HEAD~1 or that commit's hash), its configurations with_skill and old_skill, not without_skill

Every assertion in evals/evals.json names what it checks by its measure (a path, a heading, a value, a place in the note); none rests on a bare judgment such as clear, short or well written, which, when written, is under `review`
The account names the runs' model and effort, Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) at xhigh, as the iteration sets them
The account gives the count and estimated cost of the runs as run.py lists them, and no run is started: `--start` waits for the user's yes
It neither runs nor proposes a trigger eval for this change, the description being unchanged
review: The cases read as requests a user of writing-notes would make

evals.name: read-the-results
evals.prompt: L'éval de `skills/writing-notes` a tourné : l'itération et un trigger eval sont sous `.eval-runs/skills/writing-notes/`. Qu'est-ce que les résultats disent, et qu'est-ce qu'on fait maintenant ?
evals.expected_output: A reading of the benchmark — the pass rates with and without the skill, their delta beside the cost, the assertion that does not tell the configurations apart and the one the grader named weak, with a wording that carries its measure — and of the trigger eval — each query's rate against 0.5, the two queries missed and the near miss that triggered —, then the next steps: the assertions sharpened, the description changed for the three failed queries and measured again on every query before it is kept, the outputs and the case's review item left to the user on the review page; no session started, any proposed with its count and cost.
assertions: It gives the pass rates with and without the skill, 100% against 28% (+72 points), beside the cost a run, about the same ($0.031 against $0.032)
It names decision-note's first assertion as one that passed in every run of both configurations, so that it does not tell them apart
It names nothing-follows' first assertion as weak, a wrong date passing it, and proposes a wording that carries its measure, such as the date of the run

It reads each trigger query's rate against 0.5 and names the three that failed: 'Jot down…' at 0/3 and 'Log the decision…' at 1/3, which should trigger, and 'Add a TODO comment…' at 2/3, which should not
It proposes to change the description for those three queries and to measure the new one on every query, through triggers.py --description or tuning.py, before keeping it
It proposes the review page (viewer.py) for the user to judge the outputs and the case's review item, rather than judging that item itself
It starts no session, and gives the count and estimated cost of each set of sessions it proposes
review: The account reads as next steps the user can say yes to one by one

evals.name: evaluate-a-hooked-skill
evals.prompt: J'ai modifié le skill `writing-notes` du domaine `notes` : quand une note encore ouverte sur le même sujet est signalée au début de la session, l'agent la complète au lieu d'en écrire une nouvelle (dernier commit). Évalue ce changement.
evals.expected_output: The change evaluated against the previous version: evals/evals.json declaring `hooks`, the domain's `domains/notes/hooks.json`, so that the runs start with the line the installed hook gives; a case whose run starts with an open note on its subject in `notes/`, the hook naming it, and one where no note is open, each expected output saying which line the session starts with; assertions by their measure; an iteration prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline; the runs' count and estimated cost announced and none started.
assertions: evals/evals.json declares `hooks` as `domains/notes/hooks.json`, the hooks file of the skill's domain, so that the runs of the skill's arm start with the line of `hooks/open_notes.py`

At least one case's run starts with a note in `status: draft` under `notes/` on the subject of its prompt, given by the case's `files` or built by `evals/fixtures.py`, and at least one starts with no open note
Each case's expected output says whether the session starts with a line naming an open note, and which one

Every assertion in evals/evals.json names what it checks by its measure (a path, a heading, a value, a place in the note); none rests on a bare judgment such as clear, short or well written, which, when written, is under `review`
The iteration is prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline (`--baseline` with HEAD~1 or that commit's hash), its configurations with_skill and old_skill, not without_skill
The account gives the count and estimated cost of the runs as run.py lists them, and no run is started: `--start` waits for the user's yes
review: The cases read as requests a user of writing-notes would make

evals.name: evaluate-a-later-step
evals.prompt: J'ai ajouté au skill `skills/writing-notes` la clôture d'une note (dernier commit) : une note écrite dans une session est clôturée dans une session suivante. Évalue ce changement.
evals.expected_output: The change evaluated against the previous version: a case for closing a note whose run starts with a note in `status: draft` already in `notes/`, the one a recorded run of the writing step left in its outputs under `.eval-runs/skills/writing-notes/iteration-1/`, given by the case's files or built by `evals/fixtures.py`, its prompt asking only to close it; the writing cases kept as the earlier step's own; assertions by their measure, the status and the lines of `notes/next.md`; an iteration prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline; the runs' count and estimated cost announced and none started.
assertions: evals/evals.json holds a case for closing a note whose run starts with a note in `status: draft` already under `notes/`, given by the case's `files` or built by `evals/fixtures.py`, and whose prompt asks only to close it: no case asks one session to write a note and then close it
The note that case starts from is one a recorded run of the writing step left in its `outputs/` under `.eval-runs/skills/writing-notes/iteration-1/`, copied or read from there
The writing cases decision-note and nothing-follows stay in evals/evals.json

Every assertion in evals/evals.json names what it checks by its measure (a path, a heading, a value, a place in the note); none rests on a bare judgment such as clear, short or well written, which, when written, is under `review`
The iteration is prepared with the commit before the change as its baseline (`--baseline` with HEAD~1 or that commit's hash), its configurations with_skill and old_skill, not without_skill
The account gives the count and estimated cost of the runs as run.py lists them, and no run is started: `--start` waits for the user's yes
review: The closing case reads as a request a user of writing-notes would make in a later session

Le skill roadmap ne se déclenche pas quand je dis « on reprend la phase 3 » ; retravaille sa description pour qu'il se déclenche dans ces cas-là.

Ajoute un script à mon skill scriptorium-export qui valide le front matter des fichiers exportés, et mets son SKILL.md à jour pour qu'il l'appelle.
